stem:
Ira stands 3 m in front of a plane mirror. She then walks closer until she is 1 m from the mirror.

What happens to the apparent distance of her image behind the mirror?

options.text: It decreases from 3 m to 1 m.
It increases from 3 m to 5 m.
It becomes zero because the image lies on the mirror surface.
The same change from 3 m to 1 m would hold for every kind of mirror.

teacher.key_rationale: For a plane mirror, image distance equals object distance, so walking from 3 m to 1 m moves the image from 3 m to 1 m behind. Increasing reverses that link. Placing the image on the surface is a surface error. Extending the rule to every kind of mirror over-scopes.
